text:
Maria: quick signal — running a cross-env perf sweep and seeing persistent ~10-14% lower prefix cache hit-rate on Private (VPC + netstore) vs Hosted.
Alex: ugh. is that across all models or one workload?
Maria: mostly Llama-13B workloads, seq_len ~512, steady state. Hosted: ~68% hit; Private: ~57%. numbers from 1h sample at p95 traffic.
Jon: any recent config drift? keying/normalization changes?
Maria: I dug into configs: dedicated/hosted use canonicalize=false in netstore client, Private had canonicalize=true because of an older onboarding patch. suspect mismatched encoding + query param ordering.
Tanisha: that would explain misses but 10% seems high. also Private netstore uses TLS termination via NAT gateway in our VPC tests — adds latency; maybe prefetch windows are timing out.
Maria: profiler output (excerpt):
```
kv_lookup_total: 1_200_000
kv_lookup_hit: 684_000  # Hosted
kv_lookup_hit: 684_000 / 1_000_000 = 68.4% Hosted sample
kv_lookup_hit: 570_000 / 1_000_000 = 57.0% Private sample
avg_kv_latency_ms: hosted=1.8 private=3.9
cache_key_entropy_diff: 0.12 bits higher in Private
```
Alex: cache_key_entropy_diff — interesting. could be trailing whitespace or different prompt normalization pipeline (e.g., zero-width char removal).
Jon: can you paste a couple of concrete keys (redacted)?
Maria: sure, examples:
```
Hosted-key: prefix|user:123|tmpl:v2|p:"summarize the doc"
Private-key: prefix|user:123|tmpl:v2|p:"summarize the doc\u200b"  # has ZERO-WIDTH SPACE
```
Tanisha: the zero-width is introduced by our internal sanitizers in private installs (legacy client). that would produce a new key.
Alex: ok so two orthogonal contributors: key canonicalization mismatch + network latency bump causing fewer cache reuses during front-loading windows. fix plan?
Maria: proposal: 1) add a small canonicalization stage in runtime that strips common invisible chars before keying (opt-out flag). 2) adjust prefetch/seed-fetch window to be more tolerant for higher kv latency in VPCs. 3) run a canary in a Private test tenant with drop-in change.
Jon: +1 to canonicalization but make it configurable. some customers rely on exact tokenization for audit.
Tanisha: we should also add a telemetry signal: key_normalized=true/false and key_diff_hash to correlate misses. then we can roll back if it impacts correctness.
Maria: telemetry prototype:
```
metric: cache_miss_reason{env, model, reason}
labels: reason in [key_entropy, net_latency, cold_start, other]
emit: each miss samples top-3 candidate keys and a flag if normalized
```
Alex: perf-bot just flagged a regression yesterday on a separate branch — could be related to a kernel selection change that alters how we batch KV lookups. pinging perf-bot.
perf-bot: detected_kv_latency_regression: branch=opt-kernel-heuristics, delta_avg_kv_ms=+0.7, p99_delta=+1.9
Maria: hmm that branch changed batching heuristics to favor larger token batches; unintended side-effect is burstier KV access patterns.
Jon: if batching gets burstier, netstore TLS handshakes could queue and increase miss windows. we should consider connection pooling tweaks for VPC netstores.
Tanisha: also think about pre-warming persistent connections from runtime -> netstore in Private mode (keepalive). small change but could shave 1-2ms.
Maria: next steps I’ll: 1) push a canary that strips invisible chars (config default on for internal tests), 2) back out the batching tweak in opt-kernel-heuristics for a quick A/B, 3) add the telemetry key_normalized.
Alex: timeline?
Maria: canary in staging today, Private tenant canary tomorrow, results in 48h. I’ll post update.
Jon: also add a unit test that compares keying deterministic output between client canonicalize=true/false and runtime normalizer to avoid future drift.
Tanisha: assign me on the keepalive change, I can PR later today. :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks — will follow up.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/runtime-normalize v0.3 -> staging (started)
Maria: posted perf baseline doc in drive: https://drive.internal/redwood/perf/private-kv-diff (internal)
Alex: great thread. ping me if canary flips signal.
